why: A skipped test is counted in the same line as a passing one, in a colour nobody reads. A test that skips in EVERY job of the pipeline therefore looks, in every report, exactly like a test that holds — and it holds nothing. This file is the decision about which skips are real capability gates and which job supplies the capability.

`runs_in` is the load-bearing field, and there is no value for it meaning 'nowhere'. Naming a job is a claim, and .github/scripts/skip-budget.py verifies the claim IN that job: the file has to be collected there and skip nothing there. A gate that no job can answer is not pinnable, so it has to be fixed.

`markers` counts the `markTestSkipped(` and `->skip(` call sites in the file and is held by tests/Contracts/EverySkipNamesAJobThatRunsItArchTest.php. `skipped` counts the TESTS a job reports skipped, which differs: one marker in a beforeEach retires a whole file, and one marker on a datasetted test retires a case per row.

No entry here runs nowhere, and tests/Contracts/EverySkipNamesAJobThatRunsItArchTest.php now holds that at zero. The two that did were the Android notification activity and the iOS timezone shell, and both were wrong about what they needed: nativephp/mobile SHIPS the Android Studio and Xcode templates that native:install copies into the generated tree, so the bytes each anchor reads arrive with `composer install` in the mobile root. One reached for the generated path under the shipped root and the other for a generated tree from the wrong base; each miss read as a capability gate. They are the same shape as the `expect(true)->toBeTrue()` blocks the budget replaced — a rule that read nothing, reported in a colour nobody reads — one costume further along. `runs_in: null` with a `runs_nowhere` block naming the missing artefact and what would produce it is still a legal shape and still verified; raising the ceiling past zero is the argument to have before the next one is written down.

jobs.quality shard: ci.yml `quality shard N (PHP 8.5)` — repo-root Composer root, ubuntu-latest, every testsuite in phpunit.xml split across three runners.
jobs.mobile-app quality: ci.yml `mobile-app quality (PHP 8.5)` — the mobile-app/ Composer root, where nativephp/mobile and the paid plugins are installed. Runs the Mobile testsuite only.
jobs.docs-symbol (both roots): ci.yml `mobile-app quality (PHP 8.5)`, the step that runs one file from the REPO root after installing both roots — the only context in which both classmaps exist.

Modules/Auth/tests/Feature/RecoveryCodes.why: Gated on the `mobile.recovery-codes.export` route. Modules/Mobile/Routes/web.php registers it unconditionally and the Mobile module is enabled in both roots, so the gate is answered everywhere and these never actually skip.

Modules/Core/tests/Feature/Bootstrap/App.why: Gated on not being root, for the same reason as the two Receipts entries below: both cases work by taking write permission off a directory, and root ignores that. The GitHub runner executes steps as the unprivileged `runner` user, so neither skips there.

Modules/Core/tests/Feature/EncryptedBack.why: Gated on SQLite3::backup(), which ext-sqlite3 has had since PHP 7.4. Present on every runner the pipeline uses.

Modules/Core/tests/Feature/HostPipeWatch.why: The one marker left guards proc_open failing, which does not happen on the runner. A second used to sit on the no-host-pipe assertion and read the RUNNER's own stdin: a paratest worker is spawned with a pipe on every descriptor, so under --parallel — which is how every job runs — that assertion skipped everywhere. The probe now builds the no-host case in a child given /dev/null, so there is nothing left to gate on.

Modules/Core/tests/Unit/NativeZipWriterT.why: Gated on a system `unzip` to verify the archive with; ubuntu-latest ships one.

Modules/Desktop/tests/Feature/AListenerS.why: Gated on binding the LAN sync port, which is free on the runner.

Modules/Desktop/tests/Feature/RelayProvi.why: Gated on a routable LAN address. A GitHub-hosted runner has a default route and a private address on it.

Modules/Desktop/tests/Feature/SyncListen.why: Gated on binding the LAN sync port, which is free on the runner.
Gated on port 51337 being bindable, which it is on the runner.

Modules/DevMode/tests/Feature/ACountedPh.why: Gated on the browser plural probe and the node module it runs. Every job that runs tests does `npm ci` before Pest, so node_modules is there.

Modules/DevMode/tests/Feature/AFinishedR.why: Gated on ext-posix, which the Linux PHP builds setup-php installs enable by default.

Modules/DevMode/tests/Feature/PaletteMat.why: Gated on node_modules being installed. The shard job runs `npm ci --ignore-scripts` before Pest because the Vite manifest is needed for view rendering, and that install is what answers this gate too.

Modules/Import/tests/Feature/ImportStagi.why: Gated on the filesystem reporting inodes; the runner's ext4 root does.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Feature/AppShellScr.why: beforeEach requires Native\Mobile\Testing\Native. nativephp/mobile and nativephp/desktop hard-conflict, so it is installed under mobile-app/ only — one marker retires all thirteen tests in the repo-root job and all thirteen run in the mobile one.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Feature/MobileRecov.why: Gated on MobileEnsureDatabaseReady being in the web group, which mobile-app/bootstrap/app.php registers and the repo root does not.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Feature/MobileResto.why: Same gate: the route is only reachable through middleware the mobile root registers.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/ANotificationT.why: Gated on the WebView client nativephp/mobile ships. The mobile-app root installs it, and the repo root resolves it too, so the marker guards a developer checkout without the package rather than a job. It replaced an `expect(true)->toBeTrue()` that reported a pass for a rule that had read nothing.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/APostBodyIssue.why: Same gate and the same replacement: the shipped WebView client, present in both roots the pipeline builds.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/AShippedShellD.why: The case that anchors the inspection gate against the shell nativephp/mobile actually ships; the template it reads lives in that package's vendor tree, so only the mobile root can answer it. The five cases beside it patch a shell the file writes and run everywhere.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/AWebViewErrorP.why: The upstream Kotlin the patch script rewrites ships inside nativephp/mobile's vendor tree; one marker in a shared helper retires all three tests where that root is absent.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/AndroidSendsOn.why: Same gate and the same replacement: the shipped WebView client, present in both roots the pipeline builds.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/Identity/Biome.why: Beatrax\BiometricVault\BiometricVault is the first-party beatrax/mobile-biometric-vault plugin, a path package required only by the mobile-app root — not nativephp/mobile-biometrics, which is a different plugin this entry used to name. One of the two markers sits on a four-row dataset, which is why two markers report five skips.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/Identity/TheSi.why: The positive control for the `native:` prefix reads NativeActionCoordinator.kt, which ships inside nativephp/mobile and is installed only in the mobile-app root. The two name-agreement rules in the same file read tracked sources and run everywhere.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/Identity/WhatT.why: Beatrax\BiometricVault\BiometricVault is the first-party beatrax/mobile-biometric-vault plugin, a path package required only by the mobile-app root. One of the two markers sits on an eight-row dataset, which is why two markers report nine skips.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/IosBackgroundT.why: Gated on the iOS project and SchedulerManifestGenerator. Both are reachable in the two roots the pipeline builds; the markers guard a checkout that installed neither.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/NativeServiceP.why: Reads the live Native\Mobile\Edge\ElementRegistry, which only nativephp/mobile builds and which installs only under mobile-app/vendor. The desktop root has no registry to read; the mobile root is the only one where an empty plugin allow-list is visible at all.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/NoInboundDeepL.why: Reads the packager's own source out of nativephp/mobile's vendor tree.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/TheAnswerToThe.why: Ties the hand-written notification-activity fixture to the activity the build generates. It is not a build artefact: Native\Mobile\Concerns\InstallsAndroid copies vendor/nativephp/mobile/resources/androidstudio/ onto nativephp/android/, so the shipped template IS the generated file before this repo's patch scripts run. The arm reached for the GENERATED path under the SHIPPED root — an `android/` segment that exists in the copy's destination and not in its source — found nothing, and the entry recorded that miss as a capability no job here could supply. Every sibling in this directory already anchors on the same vendor tree, which the mobile root installs.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/TheBackgroundM.why: Gated on SchedulerManifestGenerator, which nativephp/mobile ships and both pipeline roots resolve.

Modules/Mobile/tests/Unit/TheZoneAnIPhon.why: Ties the hand-written iOS timezone fixture to the shell the build actually compiles. InstallsIos copies vendor/nativephp/mobile/resources/xcode/ onto nativephp/ios/, so the two Swift files these anchors name ship in the package and no native build has to run for them to be read. The arm read the generated tree instead, at `mobile-app/nativephp/...` — a path that cannot resolve from the mobile root either, where base_path() IS mobile-app. It now requires BOTH runtimes to be found, so one seam moving upstream fails rather than shortening the loop.

Modules/Receipts/tests/Feature/ScanInbox.why: Gated on a non-root euid, because chmod does not restrain root. The GitHub runner executes steps as the unprivileged `runner` user.

Modules/Receipts/tests/Unit/Pipeline/Fil.why: Gated on the filesystem exposing POSIX mode bits; ext4 does.
Gated on not being root, for the same reason as the drop-folder test above.

Modules/Sync/tests/Feature/APeerThatAnsw.why: Gated on binding the LAN sync port, which is free on the runner.

Modules/Sync/tests/Feature/DaemonDiesWit.why: Gated on proc_open succeeding, which it does on the runner.

Modules/Sync/tests/Feature/LocalRelayPro.why: Gated on a routable LAN address, which the runner has — the same gate the Desktop relay test passes.

Modules/Sync/tests/Unit/MdnsAdvertiserCa.why: Gated on dns-sd or avahi-publish-service being on the host, and ubuntu-latest shipped neither — so it skipped in every job. The shard and coverage runners now install avahi-utils alongside poppler-utils; the binary is all the advertiser looks for.

tests/Contracts/AShippedDistImportsAFile.why: Both markers are gated on vendor/nativephp/desktop being installed, which every repo-root job installs from the lock. Not listed for the mobile-app job, which runs the Mobile testsuite only and never collects tests/Contracts — and which could not answer this one anyway, because nativephp/mobile and nativephp/desktop hard-conflict.

tests/Contracts/AStoreShapeIsBuiltBeside.why: Both Composer roots run this file and only the repo root has the workflows beside it. Both markers guard the same absence and both RUN in the quality shard, which is why the zero pinned there still answers for the file. Not listed for the mobile-app job, which runs the Mobile testsuite only and never collects tests/Contracts.

tests/Contracts/BoundaryArchTest.php.why: Sixteen module-scoped rules each gated on their module's directory. Every module is present in the repo root, so none of them fires there; they replaced `expect(true)->toBeTrue()` blocks that reported a pass for a rule that had read nothing. Not listed for the mobile-app job, which never collects tests/Contracts.

tests/Contracts/ChartAxisMoneyFollowsRea.why: Gated on ICU carrying nl data, which excuses the English-only mobile PHP build. The CI runner's ext-intl carries the full set.

tests/Contracts/DocsNameSymbolsThatExist.why: Reads BOTH roots' optimised classmaps, because a class one root never loads still exists. No job had both installed, so it skipped in 100% of runs while reporting green; the mobile job now installs the repo root as well and runs this one file from there. This is the failure this whole budget generalises.
